question: Measure Schedule C lobbying reporting in the small-recipient tail: draw a stratified random sample (by sponsor segment and NTEE group) of ~2,000 of the 154,570 top-50 Schedule I recipient EINs below the P-NEW-ADV-01 fetch cap ($11.5bn, 14.7% of net FY2023-24 dollars), parse their TY2023-2024 Form 990/990-EZ Part IV and Schedule C, and replace the 30.0%-58.8% bounds on the all-dollar lobbying share with a point estimate
conclusion_affected: Completes the descriptive picture of recipient lobbying reporting for all DAF grant dollars rather than the 71% covered
rationale: Among covered recipients 20% report lobbying by count but 42% by dollars, so the uncovered tail of small recipients likely has a lower share; a sample of public IRS e-file XML (about 1 minute of fetches) would quantify it

question: Separate own lobbying from regranting for lobbying among DAF grant recipients: for the 2,602 covered recipients reporting lobbying, split Schedule C Part II-B line 1j into line 1f (grants to other organisations for lobbying) and direct activity, and tag fiscal sponsors/intermediaries (NTEE T/U/W, Schedule I grant intensity); report the share of DAF dollars to recipients whose reported lobbying is mainly regranting
conclusion_affected: Whether recipient lobbying intensity figures are driven by a few intermediaries; affects how a DAF platform describes recipient profiles neutrally
rationale: Excluding the 10 largest recipients removes $0.43bn from the 5-20% intensity band, all from one intermediary whose Part II-B total is mostly line 1f grants; the parsed-value cache already holds the line items

question: Data-quality check of 501(c)(3) political-activity disclosures and 501(h) entries among DAF grant recipients: for the 36 covered recipients ($73.5m) with Form 990 Part IV line 3 'Yes' or a positive Schedule C Part I amount, and the 28 electors whose lobbying exceeds the single-year nontaxable amount, read Schedule C Part I-A/II-A and Schedule O text and adjacent-year or amended returns to classify each as an entry error (e.g. lobbying entered in Part I-A, line 1e = line 1c) or a substantive disclosure
conclusion_affected: Size of self-reporting error in Schedule C fields that recipient-screening tools (and a DAF entrant's grant rail) might surface to donors
rationale: Part I-A entries co-occur with lobbying in 26 of the 36 cases and only 7 have both a Part IV 'Yes' and a Part I amount; 18 of the 28 elector excesses show line 1e <= line 1c, suggesting form-entry errors rather than activity of that size
